CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, persistent fatigue, sleep quality, and headache frequency.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment regarding his ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, and tension-type headaches. He reports that the adjustments made to his medication regimen have yielded mixed results. While he continues to benefit from the Melatonin 5 mg nightly, which has helped him achieve approximately seven hours of sleep per night, he still experiences occasional difficulty falling asleep, particularly during periods of heightened anxiety related to work stressors.
Mr. Smith expresses frustration regarding his persistent fatigue, which he now feels is compounded by his increased workload as the school year progresses. He describes episodes of significant daytime drowsiness, particularly after lunch, which he attributes to both his anxiety and disrupted sleep patterns.
Regarding his headaches, he reports that the frequency remains stable at four episodes per week, but the intensity of the headaches has not improved. He notes that the headaches are often accompanied by photophobia and phonophobia, which have become more pronounced. He continues to use Ibuprofen three times a week, but he states that the relief is only temporary and insufficient for managing the increased severity of his headaches.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General: Persistent fatigue; reports no significant weight changes. Cardiovascular: Intermittent palpitations stable; denies chest pain or edema. Respiratory: No shortness of breath; CPAP compliance noted; no cough or wheezing. Gastrointestinal: Mild nausea persists; occasional bloating; no vomiting or changes in bowel habits. Neurological: Increased headache intensity with photophobia and phonophobia; no focal neurological deficits.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Mild obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed on sleep study. - Tension-type headaches.
FAMILY HISTORY
- Father: Coronary artery disease, underwent CABG at age 60. - Mother: Hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
- Lives alone in , . Works as a teacher. No tobacco use; social alcohol consumption. No illicit drug use.
MEDICATIONS
- Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. - Magnesium supplement 400 mg daily. - Melatonin 5 mg nightly. - Escitalopram 30 mg daily. - Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly. - CPAP machine for sleep apnea.
ALLERGIES
- No known drug allergies.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
VITALS: T 98.6F, HR 78 bpm, BP 120/76 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, O2 sat 94% on room air.
General: Well-nourished, alert, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. No peripheral edema. Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; CPAP device noted, no wheezing or crackles. Gastrointestinal: Soft, non-tender abdomen; no epigastric tenderness. Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no focal deficits. Moderate tenderness noted on palpation of the bilateral temporalis region.
LABORATORY DATA
Lipid Panel (obtained at last visit): Total Cholesterol 160 mg/dL, LDL 80 mg/dL, HDL 62 mg/dL, Triglycerides 85 mg/dL CBC: Normal BMP: Normal TSH: Normal
RADIOLOGICAL STUDIES
- No new studies indicated at this visit.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Persistent fatigue and sleep disturbances with ongoing anxiety. - Mr. Smith continues to report improved sleep quality with Melatonin but expresses concerns regarding persistent fatigue and anxiety. We will maintain the current regimen of Melatonin 5 mg nightly and Escitalopram 30 mg daily. Due to the ongoing intensity of his headaches and sleep challenges, we will increase Amitriptyline to 15 mg nightly. Reassess CPAP therapy efficacy and consider a follow-up sleep study if symptoms do not improve. Encourage continued adherence to sleep hygiene practices and gradual exercise. Schedule follow-up in 4 weeks to monitor progress.
2. Stable frequency and increased intensity of tension-type headaches. - The patient reports stable headache frequency but increased intensity with photophobia and phonophobia. We will increase Amitriptyline to 15 mg nightly and consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation if headaches do not improve. Follow-up in 4 weeks to reassess headache frequency and severity.
3. Lipid management. - Continue Atorvastatin 10 mg daily as lipid levels remain stable. Reassess lipid panel in 3 months to evaluate ongoing effectiveness.
4. Follow-up. - Schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to reassess anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, headache frequency, and overall well-being. Discuss potential referrals for cognitive-behavioral therapy if anxiety symptoms persist or worsen.
